messages:
maria.k: Quick follow-up to the RFC discussion from last week — we need a concrete pattern for cross-project service auth. Do we prefer scoped API keys, service-account impersonation, or JWT delegation for internal services?
ajay: TL;DR: prefer short-lived impersonation tokens if latency and opa checks are OK. Scoped API keys are easier for external partners.
sarah: Agree with ajay. For internal-to-internal calls, impersonation + aud/iss checks gives clearer audit trail. For public/private partner integrations, scoped API keys with proper rotation make onboarding simpler.
maria.k: Two practical worries: 1) rollout complexity (we have dozens of downstream projects) 2) monitoring — can we tag calls with originating project id so billing/audit works?
kevin: For rollout, we can implement a proxy that handles impersonation for legacy clients. Proxy injects header: X-Called-By-Project: <proj-id> and we record it in access logs.
sarah: Proxy sounds fine but watch out for trust boundaries. If a proxy accepts API keys and mints tokens, we need strict mTLS + token exchange and attestation.
auth-bot: reminder: existing token lifetime defaults = 24h, rotation recommended every 12h for service tokens per policy-3.
ajay: I'd propose a hybrid pattern: - internal services use short-lived impersonation tokens (1h) minted by a central token service (mTLS + caller SA) - external integrations use scoped API keys with explicit project-id scope and rotation hooks (90d max)
maria.k: Hybrid seems reasonable. Two open questions: A) how do we express cross-project scopes? B) how do we migrate long-lived keys to rotation-friendly pattern without breaking CI?
kevin: A) scope model: resource://{org}/{project}/{service}:{actions} — we validate both org and project in ACL check. B) migration: add an acceptance mode where both old key and new tokens are accepted for 30 days, also emit deprecation telemetry.
sarah: On the ACL model: ensure least-privilege paths by allowing deny rules at project-level. Also add "delegation:" claim into tokens so listener can see original caller chain.
ajay: Example token flow for internal call: 1) Caller mTLSs to token service with SA cert 2) Token service validates caller SA, issues JWT with claims {iss:token-svc, sub:caller-sa, aud:service, delegation:[caller-project]} 3) Downstream enforces aud + delegation chain
maria.k: Can someone write a tiny authz example for the SDKs? e.g., header usage, sample claims. We can put it in RFC follow-up.
kevin: sample header: Authorization: Bearer <jwt> ; sample claim snippet: {"iss":"token-svc","sub":"svc-account@proj-123","aud":"ingest-service","delegation":["proj-123"]}
auth-bot: note: cluster policy requires token introspection for >5s requests, add caching layer for introspection results.
ajay: For auditing, ensure token id (jti) is logged and linked to span ids so we can query traces by token. Also add a lightweight anomaly signal if same token used from multiple regions simultaneously.
maria.k: Ok action items: (1) kevin to draft SDK header usage + migration plan (2) sarah to write attestation and mTLS requirements (3) ajay to update token-service flow and TTLs in RFC. I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
kevin: got it, I'll post the draft in #eng-security by EOD tomorrow.
sarah: I'll update the security checklist, ping when draft is ready.
ajay: Leaving a note: we should run a tabletop for the proxy scenario before prod rollout.
maria.k: Agreed. Closing thread for now, we'll reconvene after the drafts.
